placements.why: The document's whole contribution is a delivery-routing decision: every reaction routed through one bundle per run per person rather than one message per skill (src-2), the bundle closing when the run closes with late skills waiting for the next run rather than sending on their own (src-4), and the displaced alternative — per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the reader (src-5). The position pass holds these three as one settled position, DeliveryRoutingPerRunBundle. This is a subject, not a fact: how a run's output reaches a person is a standing product rule future envelopes will keep feeding, so it passes the grain test and mints. Nothing in the supplied structure covers delivery routing — Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning is a positioning thesis, Narrative_DecisionsEvaporate a problem narrative, Narrative_DecisionCaptureAtConsensus a capture-at-consensus insight — so no exact `under` exists; the new leaf is understood in relation to the anti-Slack thesis (structured async over real-time noise) via `see`, since batching delivery to the reader's run is that stance expressed at the delivery layer, but it is not a child of it.
placements.title: Delivery batches to the reader's run, not the skill's moment
placements.frame: When a run produces several reactions for one person, what does that person receive — one bundle at the run's close, or a message per skill as each finishes?
